papers.title: Dioptra-DINO: Real-Time Monocular Metric Depth Estimation via Canonical Virtual Camera Normalization for Edge Robotics
papers.summary: Monocular metric depth estimation on autonomous mobile robots presents an acute trade-off between physical scale fidelity and closed-loop inference latency. Contemporary metric vision foundation models (e.g., UniDepth V2, Metric3D) achieve impressive zero-shot transfer, but their high computational footprints (400–750 ms per frame) limit throughput to 1.3–2.4 FPS on embedded hardware, inducing unacceptable control latency for aerial navigation and quadrupedal locomotion (where >15 FPS is typically targeted for closed-loop stability). papers.title: Performance E valuation of E xploration S trategies on L earning E fficiency and S tability in Q-Learning
papers.summary: A fundamental problem in reinforcement learning is the trade-off between exploration and exploitation. The quality of the final policy is not the only factor that varies with different exploration strategies, so do learning speed and result stability. Based on Q-learning, this study compares three exploration strategies in a custom 5×5 GridWorld environment: fixed ε=0.10, fixed ε=0.30, and linearly decaying ε (1.00→0.05). papers.title: The Architecture of Demerzel: What Asimov Hid Inside the Three Laws
papers.summary: Isaac Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics are the most widely cited governance framework in the history of artificial intelligence. They appear in congressional testimony, United Nations white papers, and the opening paragraphs of national AI strategies worldwide. They are also incomplete — and Asimov knew it. This book traces what Asimov actually built across forty years of fiction: not a solution to machine governance, but a curriculum designed to expose its absence. papers.title: ECPR for cardiac arrest caused by postoperative massive pulmonary embolism in a super-morbidly obese patient: A case report
papers.summary: Background: Massive pulmonary embolism (PE) remains a leading cause of preventable perioperative mortality after bariatric surgery. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is challenging in patients with extreme obesity, and extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) is increasingly used as a salvage therapy. Where and how this transformation emerges along the somatosensory axis from peripheral proprioceptive receptors remains unclear. Kalunga2016 – SSVEP Exo dataset
papers.summary: This dataset contains 8-channel EEG recordings from 12 healthy participants performing an SSVEP-based brain-computer interface task, originally collected for an online, asynchronous BCI for assistive robotics using an exoskeleton-equipped wheelchair. Participants focused on LEDs flickering at 13, 17 and 21 Hz, or on a fixation point for a rest (reject) class, following auditory cues. The data are provided in BIDS format, converted via MOABB from the original Zenodo deposit.

papers.title: Motor Imagery ataset from Ofner et al 2017
papers.summary: EEG recordings from fifteen healthy participants who executed and imagined six sustained upper limb movements (elbow flexion/extension, forearm supination/pronation, hand open/close) plus a rest condition, in two separate sessions. The dataset supports decoding of single upper limb movements from the time-domain of low-frequency EEG. It is relevant to non-invasive control of motor neuroprostheses and robotic arms. This BIDS version was generated from the original BNCI Horizon 2020 data using MOABB.

papers.title: Sensor-driven evolutionary optimisation of mobile robot controllers using enzymatic numerical P systems
papers.summary: Abstract In recent years, the application of membrane computing within the field of robotics has been widely investigated, providing a bio-inspired alternative to traditional control paradigms. This paper proposes an approach that combines Enzymatic Numerical P Systems (ENPS) with Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm (NSGA-II), a well-known multi-objective evolutionary optimisation algorithm, as core components of a real-time obstacle avoidance robot controller. papers.title: Investigation of FBG Accelerometers and Load Sensors for Vibration Analysis and Slip Detection in Robotic Manipulators
papers.summary: This paper presents an investigation of the viability of Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) accelerometers and load sensors for two diagnostic tasks in robotics: vibration analysis of industrial manipulators and slip detection in robotic grippers. The study synthesizes experimental results from two independent experiments, focusing on the use of optical sensors in place of traditional electromechanical devices such as MEMS accelerometers and resistive strain gauges. papers.title: Theoretical Design and Computational Projections for the VESPA V7 Integrated Bio-Hybrid Cartridge System
papers.summary: This repository contains the conceptual design document and theoretical engineering framework for the VESPA V7 Integrated Bio-Hybrid Cartridge, a 2 kg modular platform engineered to achieve 30 months of autonomous operation through a multi-tier decoupling strategy. papers.title: AI-Powered Robotics for Reliable, Stable, and Robust Operation and Maintenance of Power Systems: Architecture, Unified Modeling, and Quantitative Evaluation
papers.summary: Abstract Robotic inspection and artificial intelligence (AI) are increasingly used in power-system operation and maintenance (O&M), yet they are usually evaluated in isolation—by image-detection accuracy or robot mobility—rather than by their effect on the quantities utilities are regulated on. The inspection of O&G plants' equipment is a concrete commitment reflected in standard maintenance plans. papers.title: Real-Time Robotic Inspection: A Game-Changing Solution to Prevent Production Loss and Extend Lifetime Well
papers.summary: Abstract The Cepu field continues to face recurring tubing failures in sucker-rod wells due to localized internal wear on reused tubing. Conventional inspection using Ultrasonic Testing (UT), performed at only 12 points per joint, fails to detect thinning that occurs between measurement locations. In 2024, tubing leaks accounted for 74% of total failure-related losses during well service activities, resulting in USD 420,930.40 in Loss Production Opportunity (LPO). papers.title: Ultrastable Wide-Range Capacitive Pressure Sensors with CNTs-Pinned PDMS Foam Composite Dielectrics for Intelligent Tactile Perception
papers.summary: Abstract Flexible capacitive pressure sensors have attracted considerable attention for wearable electronics, intelligent robotics, and human-machine interfaces, yet achieving high sensitivity, broad pressure detection, and long-term stability remains challenging. Herein, carbon nanotubes (CNTs)-pinned porous polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) foam composite dielectrics are developed via a facile one-step emulsion-templating strategy. papers.title: A Digital Twin Framework for Autonomous Kinetic Facades: Bio-inspired SMA Actuation with Reinforcement Learning Control for Tropical Climates
papers.summary: Building envelope automation is limited by heavy motor-driven shading and reactive rule-based controllers. This paper presents an autonomous Digital Twin framework for kinetic facades, integrating bio-inspired Shape-Memory Alloy [SMA] actuation with a Reinforcement Learning [RL] control policy. papers.title: Diffusion models in robotics: a comprehensive review
papers.summary: Diffusion models are a powerful class of generative models that emerge in recent years to transform Gaussian noise into samples of the target distribution through an iterative denoising process. papers.title: Motor imagery BCI dataset with pupillometry augmentation
papers.summary: EEG recordings from 30 healthy participants performing a left-hand grasping motor imagery task versus rest, cued by auditory stimuli, with simultaneous pupillometry. The dataset was recorded with a 32-channel BioSemi ActiveTwo system at 512 Hz across two runs of 25 trials per subject. It supports evaluating whether task-evoked pupil diameter changes can improve EEG-based motor imagery brain-computer interface classification.

papers.title: Hybrid EEG-fNIRS MI dataset for ICH from Shi et al 2025
papers.summary: A hybrid EEG-fNIRS motor imagery dataset for brain-computer interface research in intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). It includes 37 participants (17 healthy, 20 ICH patients) performing two-class left/right hand grasping motor imagery across up to several sessions. The data are pre-epoched, and the dataset is intended for developing and benchmarking BCI approaches for stroke rehabilitation.

papers.title: SCRAMBLE: Safe Cooperative Risk-Aware Multi-Agent Belief Learning for Embodied Reinforcement Learning in Partially Observable Dynamic Environments
papers.summary: Safe decision-making in partially observable dynamic environments remains a fundamental challenge for multi-agent embodied reinforcement learning, where agents must cooperate with limited local observations while responding to evolving environmental changes and safety-critical interactions. Existing methods often emphasize coordination efficiency or reward maximization, but they are less effective at jointly handling latent state uncertainty, dynamic non-stationarity, and safety constraints in a unified learning framework.
